config.title: Simple Todo List

intro.title: Simple Todo List
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple todo list application using React. You will learn how to manage a list of tasks using React state, allowing you to add new items and mark them as complete. The core programming concepts covered include handling user input with event handlers and updating the UI dynamically based on state changes. You will work with key React constructs like the useState hook, JSX for rendering, and event handling in a functional component. By the end, you will have a working interactive todo list that demonstrates fundamental React patterns.
intro.usecase: Todo lists are foundational UI patterns found in countless real-world applications. You'll see similar interfaces in project management tools like Trello or Asana for tracking tasks, in e-commerce sites for managing shopping carts, and in content management systems for handling draft articles or pending reviews. As a developer, you'll frequently build interfaces where users need to add, view, and remove items - whether it's managing user accounts in admin panels, curating playlists in music apps, or organizing filters in data dashboards. Mastering this pattern gives you the skills to create interactive lists that are central to modern web applications.

objectives: Initialize and manage a state variable to store an array of todo items.
Construct a form with an input field and a button to capture new todo text.
Implement a handler function to add a new todo item to the state array.
Render a dynamic list of todo items using the map method.
Configure a delete button for each todo item to remove it from the state.
Apply conditional rendering to display a message when no todos exist.
Manipulate the state to update the todo list based on user interactions.

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the useState hook from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports for React and useState are added to the file.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite correct. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the main TodoList component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named TodoList that returns null for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to export it.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the TodoList component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named TodoList is created and exported, returning null.
successCriteria: The TodoList component is defined and exported, returning null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the TodoList component. This is the main component that will hold our todo list logic and UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created a component named TodoList that returns null. Check if you've exported it properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a functional component named TodoList that returns null. Remember to export it so it can be used elsewhere.

steps.title: Initialize state for todos
steps.instruction: Inside the TodoList component, initialize a state variable called 'todos' using useState, starting with an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The initial value should be an empty array [].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state initialization
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a state variable 'todos' ready to store todo items.
successCriteria: The component contains a state variable named 'todos' initialized with an empty array using useState.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the todos state variable.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty array [] as the initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The todos state wasn't initialized correctly. Check that you're using useState with an empty array.

steps.title: Initialize state for input text
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component, initialize a state variable called 'inputText' using useState, starting with an empty string as the initial value.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The pattern is: const [variableName, setVariableName] = useState(initialValue).
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a text input
const [name, setName] = useState('');
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have two state variables: 'todos' for the list and 'inputText' for the current text input.
successCriteria: The component contains a state variable named 'inputText' initialized with useState and an empty string initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added state to track the input text. This will allow you to capture what the user types before adding it as a todo.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the exact variable name 'inputText' and initializing it with an empty string.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Remember to use the useState hook to create a state variable called 'inputText' starting as an empty string.

steps.title: Create handler for input change
steps.instruction: Inside your TodoList component, define a function called handleInputChange that takes an event parameter and updates the inputText state with the event's target value.
steps.hint: The function should use setInputText to update the state with event.target.value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleInputChange function is defined that updates the inputText state when called with an event object.
successCriteria: The component contains a function named handleInputChange that calls setInputText with event.target.value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the input change handler. This function will capture what the user types and update the state accordingly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function is named handleInputChange and it updates the inputText state using setInputText(event.target.value).
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a function called handleInputChange that takes an event parameter and updates the inputText state with event.target.value.

steps.title: Create handler to add a new todo
steps.instruction: Define a function called handleAddTodo inside your TodoList component. This function should add a new todo object to the todos array and clear the inputText state.
steps.hint: Inside the component, create a function that uses setTodos to update the array and setInputText to clear the input field.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleAddTodo function is defined that adds a new todo object to the todos array and resets inputText to an empty string.
successCriteria: The handleAddTodo function is defined, uses setTodos to update the todos array with a new todo object, and uses setInputText to clear the input.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handler function to add new todos and clear the input.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it updates both the todos array and clears the inputText state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleAddTodo function is not defined correctly. It should update the todos array and reset inputText.

steps.title: Return the main JSX structure
steps.instruction: In your TodoList component, return a div element with the class name 'todo-container' as the main JSX structure.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div that has a className attribute set to 'todo-container'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TodoList component now returns a div with class 'todo-container' as its main structure.
successCriteria: The component returns a div element with className="todo-container".
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've set up the main container for your todo list app.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a div with exactly className="todo-container".
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're returning a div element with the correct class name.

steps.title: Add input and button for adding todos
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement of your TodoList component, add an input element and a button element. Set the input's value attribute to inputText and its onChange handler to handleInputChange. Set the button's onClick handler to handleAddTodo.
steps.hint: Remember to use JSX syntax for the elements and curly braces for JavaScript expressions like attribute values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now have a controlled input field and a button for adding todos, though the handlers are not yet defined.
successCriteria: The return statement contains an input element with value={inputText} and onChange={handleInputChange}, and a button element with onClick={handleAddTodo}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the input and button elements with the correct attributes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the elements, but check that the input has both value and onChange attributes, and the button has onClick.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input and button elements are missing or incorrectly configured. Review the instruction and try again.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the list of todos using map. Each todo is now displayed as a list item.

steps.title: Export the TodoList component
steps.instruction: Export the TodoList component as the default export so it can be used in other files.
steps.hint: Add an export statement at the end of your file. You can use 'export default' followed by the component name.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: exporting a component
export default MyComponent;
steps.expectedOutcome: The TodoList component is exported as the default export, making it available for use in other modules.
successCriteria: The TodoList component is exported as the default export.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the TodoList component. This makes it ready to be imported and used in other files.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using 'export default' followed by the component name (TodoList).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't exported correctly. You need to add an export statement at the end of the file.
